Part of @biorate/hygen — a fork of jondot/hygen (v6.2.11, MIT), adapted to the @biorate/* monorepo. Rewritten for this fork's semantics; see Differences from upstream.

Based on: Upstream templates reference

Templates

A hygen template is a YAML frontmatter header plus an EJS body. The frontmatter describes what to do (write, inject, run a shell command); the body is the content that gets rendered and applied.

---
to: app/emails/<%= name %>.html
---
Hello <%= name %>,
<%= message %>
(version <%= version %>)

Because both the frontmatter and the body are rendered by the same EJS engine, the to: path, the values and the content can all be interpolated.

Frontmatter​

The frontmatter is delimited by a matching --- top and bottom with YAML in it. It is rendered first, so it can reference the same variables the body uses:

---
to: app/<%= section %>/emails.js
foo: <%= bar %>
---

Given the following command, the frontmatter builds behind the scenes into:

---
to: app/weekend/emails.js
foo: ping
---
hygen mailer campaign --section weekend --bar ping

Escaping semantics​

This is the single most important difference from upstream. In this fork, the <%= expr %> interpolation does not HTML-escape: the EJS escape option is the identity ((s) => s). The tool generates source code, not markup, so code passages survive verbatim:

---
to: app/compare.js
---
const cmp = <%= expr %>;
hygen sink new --expr 'a > b && c < d'
# writes: const cmp = a > b && c < d;   (no &gt; / &amp;)

The <%- expr %> tag still works and is a raw (unescaped) interpolation; in this fork <%= %> and <%- %> therefore produce the same output. Escaping is the identity for both — there is no upstream advice to "use <%- %> to avoid HTML escaping", because there is nothing to escape.

Template body​

Template bodies are EJS:

---
to: app/workers/<%= name %>.js
---
class <%= Name %> {
  work() {
    // your code here!
  }
}

The variable name is blessed: you get a capitalized version for free as Name. You can also compute derived variables inline with a <% %> scriptlet:

---
to: app/workers/<%= name %>.js
---
<%
  Message = message.toUpperCase()
%>
class <%= Name %> {
  work() {
    return "<%= Message %>";
  }
}

The same EJS engine renders both the body and the to: path.

Helpers and inflections​

The special object h hosts built-in helpers. h.capitalize uppercases the first character; h.inflection pluralizes and singularizes, and includes the fork's undasherize (kebab/snake case to KebabCase):

class <%= Name %> {
  work() {
    return "<%= h.capitalize(message) %>";
  }
}
<%= h.inflection.pluralize(name) %>
<%= h.inflection.undasherize('my-module') %><!-- MyModule -->

h.inflection exposes:

pluralize(str, plural)
singularize(str, singular)
inflect(str, count, singular, plural)
camelize(str, low_first_letter)
underscore(str, all_upper_case)
humanize(str, low_first_letter)
capitalize(str)
dasherize(str)
titleize(str)
undasherize(str)          <- fork-specific

Change-case helpers​

h.changeCase is the change-case library:

// example: <%= h.changeCase.camel(name) %>
camel(str);
constant(str);
dot(str);
header(str);
isLower(str);
isUpper(str);
lower(str);
lcFirst(str);
no(str);
param(str);
pascal(str);
path(str);
sentence(str);
snake(str);
swap(str);
title(str);
upper(str);

A typical React component generator:

---
to: components/<%= name %>/index.jsx
---
import React from 'react'

export const <%= name %> = ({ children }) => (
<div className="<%= h.changeCase.paramCase(name) %>">{children}</div>
)

With name=HelloWorld this compiles to a <div className="hello-world"> element.

h.path is the Node path module, so you can join and resolve paths inside templates.

Local variables​

Any CLI argument, positional or prompt result automatically becomes a local variable. There are two ways to refer to them:

Hello <%= message %>

The bare form refers to message; a missing value throws a reference error.

Hello <%= locals.message %>

The locals form lets you test for existence before use:

<% if (locals.message) { -%>
  message: <%= message %>
<% } -%>

The -%> slurps the trailing newline so an if clause does not leave blank lines in the output.

Predefined variables​

A command like hygen component new:story places these values into special variables:

VariableContentExample
templatesTemplates path (absolute)/project/_templates
actionfolderAction path/.../component/new
generatorGenerator namecomponent
actionAction namenew
subactionSub-action namestory
cwdProcess working directory/project
<%= actionfolder %>

Addition (add)​

By default templates are added as a new target file. The to: property tells hygen where to put it; nested directories are created automatically. force: true overwrites an existing file without prompting (the default is to prompt for confirmation).

---
to: app/index.js
force: true
---
console.log('this is index!')

To leave an existing file alone, use unless_exists: true:

---
to: app/index.js
unless_exists: true
---
will not render if target exists

skipIfExists: true is the quiet variant: an existing target is skipped without failing and without prompting (unlike force: true, which overwrites). It works on every file-creating action — plain to:, mirrored, and glob batch actions.

Glob batch actions​

A single template can scaffold a whole directory tree at once. Declare glob: with a pattern (plus base:, stripExtensions: and a to:/destination: folder) and every match becomes its own rendered file; skipIfExists: true on a batch skips a matched file whose target already exists.

See Glob batch actions for the full reference — properties, notes and examples.

Mirroring the template layout (mirror)​

A template with no to: is a no-op by default — it renders nothing and creates nothing. When you want the output path to mirror where the template lives inside the action folder, opt in with mirror: true:

---
mirror: true
---
// _templates/mailer/new/parts/header.ejs.t -> parts/header.ejs (relative to cwd)

Mirroring applies only when all three hold: mirror: true is present, there is no to:, and there is no sh attribute. The target path is the template's location inside the action folder, resolved relative to the current working directory; missing directories are created automatically.

Suffix rule​

The file-name suffix is stripped per this convention before the path is used:

SettingSource suffixTarget example
default.thtml.ejs.t → html.ejs
HYGEN_MIRROR_EJS_SUFFIX=1.ejs.thtml.ejs.t → html

The default strips a single trailing .t (so the .ejs is kept). Setting HYGEN_MIRROR_EJS_SUFFIX=1 strips the full .ejs.t instead.

Precedence and scope​

  • Explicit to: always wins — a template declaring both to: and mirror: true writes to the explicit to: target and ignores mirror.
  • sh-only templates never mirror — a template with a sh: attribute and no to: stays a no-op (no file is created), regardless of mirror.
  • Overwrite semantics are unchanged — a mirrored target behaves like any add: force: true overwrites, unless_exists: true leaves an existing file alone, and the default is to prompt for confirmation (HYGEN_OVERWRITE disables the prompt).

From & shared templates​

from: loads the body from another template instead of the body of the current file. The body of the current template is ignored:

---
to: app/readme.md
from: shared/docs/readme.md
---
THIS BODY IS IGNORED !!!

from: shared/docs/readme.md loads _templates/shared/docs/readme.md as the body of app/readme.md.

Injection​

To inject a template into an existing file, set inject: true plus exactly one anchor. The body is inserted at the resolved position. The most common guard, skip_if, prevents double injection:

---
inject: true
to: package.json
after: dependencies
skip_if: react-native-fs
---
"react-native-fs":"*",

This adds the react-native-fs dependency to package.json, but only once (the skip_if) guard sees the text already present and skips).

after: dependencies is a regular expression, so it matches the "dependencies": { block in a package.json.

Anchors (mutually exclusive)​

Exactly one of these anchor options is used per template:

  • before / after — a regular expression of text to locate. The inject line appears before or after the located line. These support multi-line matches: a single-line match is tried across each line first; if none is found, a multi-line match across the whole file is attempted.
  • prepend / append — boolean; add the body to the start or end of the file, respectively.
  • at_line — a numeric line index (0-based) at which the body is inserted. It is a line index, so it always matches.
---
inject: true
to: config.js
before: '// config'
---
custom-feature = true;

Anchor not found fails the run​

If a before/after anchor does not match (neither a single line nor the whole text), the injection throws InjectionAnchorNotFoundError, the run reports success: false, and the target file is left untouched. Unlike upstream (which silently no-ops and can even misplace the content), this fork surfaces the failure. prepend/append/at_line always have a position, so they cannot "not match".

Guarding against double injection​

  • skip_if — a regular expression / text. If it is present in the file, the injection is skipped.
  • skip_if_not: true — the pure inversion of skip_if: the injection runs only when the skip_if text/regex is present (and is skipped when it is absent). Use it to inject a block into a file that already contains a marker.

Creating a missing target​

By default, injecting into a file that does not exist is an error (InjectionTargetNotFoundError). Set create_if_missing: true to create the target (with parent folders) and then inject the body into it:

---
to: config/new.json
inject: true
create_if_missing: true
append: true
---
{ 'key': 'value' }

Replacement by anchor​

replace: true switches an inject-family operation from insert to replace: the first fragment matched by the before/after anchor is replaced by the body and the rest of the file is preserved. $ in the body is treated literally.

replace is mutually exclusive with inject (using both throws TemplateConfigError), and only before/after anchors support it (prepend/append/at_line with replace is also a TemplateConfigError). An unmatched anchor raises InjectionAnchorNotFoundError.

---
to: package.json
replace: true
after: '"version": ".*"'
---
"version": "2.0.0",

Line-ending control (eof_last)​

eof_last tunes the trailing newline of an injected body. When true, a body without a trailing newline gets one; when false, a body with a trailing newline has it removed.

Shell​

A template with sh: runs a shell command after the other actions of the run. The command is executed via the configured exec hook (execa.shell by default), with the template body piped to the command's stdin when a body is present. The cwd variable is available:

---
sh: 'mkdir -p <%= cwd %>/given/app/shell && cat > <%= cwd %>/given/app/shell/hello.piped'
---
hello, this was piped!

A shell action can be combined with an add or inject in the same template — for example, add a dependency and then run the install:

---
inject: true
to: package.json
after: dependencies
skip_if: lodash
sh: cd <%= cwd %> && npm install
---
"lodash":"*",

The body is not piped when it is absent. sh_ignore_exit: true ignores a non-zero exit; spinner: true shows a spinner during the command.

Conditional rendering​

Render a template conditionally by giving to: a value that resolves to null:

---
to: '<%= message ? `where/to/render/${name}.js` : null %>'
---
conditionally rendering template

When hygen sees a to: value of null, it skips the output of that template entirely.

Next up: generators.

Conditional action skipping (skip)​

A template can decide at render time whether it should run at all. Declare skip: in the frontmatter; it is rendered with the same locals as the template, and a truthy result skips the action — no operation executes and the run records the action as skipped. It is distinct from skipIfExists:, which reacts to an existing target on disk.

See Conditional action skipping for the full reference — the rendered value table and the notes.

PropertyTypeDefaultExample

glob:Stringundefinedmodule/**/*
base:Stringundefinedmodule
stripExtensions:String/Arrayundefined['.t']
destination:String (url)undefinedsrc/<%= name %>/
skipIfExists:Booleanfalsetrue

mirror:Booleanundefinedtrue
from:String (url)undefinedshared/docs/readme.md
